brief.summary: Pure higgsino thermal freeze-out with Sommerfeld and coannihilation corrections predicts Omega h^2 = 0.12 at m_chi ~1.0-1.2 TeV, canonically 1.1 TeV, with theoretical uncertainty from non-perturbative electroweak effects. Direct detection is dominated by Z-mediated inelastic scattering between nearly degenerate neutralinos with splitting delta ~ 100-400 keV, while Higgs-mediated elastic scattering is suppressed by high purity required by LZ 2024 and XENONnT limits. Recent work explores light-slepton coannihilation lowering the thermal mass to ~0.4-0.6 TeV and low-reheating cosmologies raising it, plus CTAO and Fermi-LAT line searches approaching the thermal annihilation cross section. The 2026 LZ 248 keV high-recoil event has renewed interest in inelastic higgsino benchmarks at 1.1 TeV and delta ~ 300-350 keV as a testable recoil-spectrum signature.

**Survey** — 30 tools on 3 servers, 5 read-only probes, 3 papers found.

Pure higgsino thermal freeze-out with Sommerfeld and coannihilation corrections predicts Omega h^2 = 0.12 at m_chi ~1.0-1.2 TeV, canonically 1.1 TeV, with theoretical uncertainty from non-perturbative electroweak effects. Direct detection is dominated by Z-mediated inelastic scattering between nearly degenerate neutralinos with splitting delta ~ 100-400 keV, while Higgs-mediated elastic scattering is suppressed by high purity required by LZ 2024 and XENONnT limits. Recent work explores light-slepton coannihilation lowering the thermal mass to ~0.4-0.6 TeV and low-reheating cosmologies raising it, plus CTAO and Fermi-LAT line searches approaching the thermal annihilation cross section. The 2026 LZ 248 keV high-recoil event has renewed interest in inelastic higgsino benchmarks at 1.1 TeV and delta ~ 300-350 keV as a testable recoil-spectrum signature.

Paper Preview Abstract Higgsino dark matter is a classic, but still viable, weakly-interacting massive particle (WIMP) scenario that could point to supersymmetry, a new spacetime symmetry of nature. It is a simple realization of the "inelastic dark matter" mechanism, where its scattering off a nucleus occurs between two nearly degenerate states. The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) collaboration has recently reported a single nuclear recoil event at a high recoil energy of about 250 keV. This has been interpreted as inelastic scattering of dark matter that is a supersymmetric Higgsino with a mass splitting between the neutral states of a few 100 keV. Such dark matter may be captured at high recoil in the Sun through scattering on heavy elements in it ... call.result: This interval covers the spectrum from the canonical thermal relic mass of ∼ 1.1 $∼1.1$ TeV down to the sub-TeV regime, allowing us to investigate the viability of lighter Higgsino dark matter. Apr 20, 2026 · While a pure Higgsino typically requires a mass of around 1.1 TeV to satisfy the observed thermal relic abundance, the presence of light sleptons can significantly alter this requirement. Dec 25, 2025 · In this work, we revisit higgsino dark matter within the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM), focusing on scenarios with slepton coannihilation. We find that efficient coannihilation allows the higgsino mass to be as light as ∼ 400 GeV while satisfying relic density constraints. May 16, 2023 · Thermal Higgsino dark matter (DM), with mass around 1 TeV, is a well-motivated, minimal DM scenario that arises in supersymmetric extensions of the standard model. We discovered that in the Higgsino DM scenario of the next-to-minimal supersymmetric model (NMSSM), the mixing of Higgsino and Singlino introduces analogous effects, with a crucial distinction being that the current LZ experiment permits significant mixing between Singlino and Higgsino. It is the aim of the present paper to verify whether attractive scenar-ios within the NMSSM exist with a correct relic den-sity, satisfying the LZ-constraints, and an additional Higgs boson with a mass of 95 GeV. We consider the long-range effect of the Higgs on the density of thermal-relic dark matter. While the electroweak gauge boson and gluon exchange have been previously studied, the Higgs is typically thought to mediate only contact interactions. call.result: In this paper, we specifically compare the prediction for the case of the thermal 1.1 TeV Higgsino with the LZ two-sided confidence interval and show that the event of interest can be accommodated by inelastic Higgsino dark matter particles. Sep 2, 2026 · As we will show in this paper, a TeV Higgsino with mass splitting around 350 keV that has inelastic spin independent scattering with the Xenon target provides a possible interpretation of the LZ event of interest. Searches for higgsinolike dark matter have significantly reduced the parameter space available where it could be directly detected easily above the neutrino fog, leaving regions with a high degree of higgsino purity and small mass splittings. One interesting remaining possibility for a WIMP is the inelastic dark matter scenario [1,2]. In this scenario, there is a small mass splitting between two nearly degenerate states, and scattering off a nucleus transitions one state to the other. Feb 10, 2022 · Split Higgsinos are a compelling class of models to explain dark matter and may be on the verge of detection by multiple current experimental avenues. The idea is based on a large split in scales between the electroweak scale and decoupled scalars, with relatively light Higgsinos between the two.

## Abstract

A pure-higgsino thermal freeze-out was examined with the inelastic-DM server tools and a survey of recent arXiv literature. The perturbative tool (Kolb & Turner 5.26-5.29, fixed g*=86.25) gives Omega h^2 = 0.0731 at 900 GeV, 0.0898 at 1000 GeV, 0.1083 at 1100 GeV, 0.1181 at 1150 GeV, 0.1202 at 1160 GeV, 0.1285 at 1200 GeV and 0.1503 at 1300 GeV, interpolating to Omega h^2 = 0.120 at 1159 GeV (1150-1170 GeV band). This is offset from the canonical literature band 1.0-1.2 TeV, canonically 1.1 TeV, which includes Sommerfeld enhancement, coannihilation and bound-state effects not in the tool. Inelastic kinematics on xenon impose delta_max ~364 keV for v_max = 776 km/s; at 1100 GeV delta = 200 keV predicts ~5.1e4 events in 2.84 tonne-yr LZ exposure while delta = 350 keV predicts ~2 events, near the kinematic limit. A 900-1300 GeV x 100-650 keV scan finds 180 of 225 points pass relic+LZ+Fermi+CMB but none predict 0.3-5 LZ events, indicating tension with a single-event interpretation. Elastic Higgs-mediated scattering must be suppressed to <1e-48 cm2 to survive LZ 2024 and XENONnT, while Z-mediated inelastic scattering is ~7.4e-39 cm2. No quantitative comparison to Fermi-LAT dwarf/GC line limits or CTAO-North sensitivity could be completed.

## Background

The literature describes pure-higgsino thermal freeze-out with Sommerfeld and coannihilation corrections predicting Omega h^2 = 0.12 at m_chi ~1.0-1.2 TeV, canonically 1.1 TeV, with theoretical uncertainty from non-perturbative electroweak effects. Direct detection is dominated by Z-mediated inelastic scattering between nearly degenerate neutralinos with splitting delta ~100-400 keV, while Higgs-mediated elastic scattering is suppressed by high purity required by LZ 2024 and XENONnT limits. Recent work explores light-slepton coannihilation lowering the thermal mass to ~0.4-0.6 TeV and low-reheating cosmologies raising it, plus CTAO and Fermi-LAT line searches approaching the thermal annihilation cross sectio

n. The 2026 LZ 248 keV high-recoil event has renewed interest in inelastic higgsino benchmarks at 1.1 TeV and delta ~300-350 keV.

Key recent papers surveyed are arXiv:2609.01504 Higgsino Above the Sea of Fog, which derives LZ/XENONnT purity bounds and defines a benchmark delta ~350 keV near the neutrino fog; arXiv:2609.04175 The Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event with the High-Energy Sideband, which interprets the 248 keV event as inelastic scattering and constrains m_chi and delta from recoil energy and sideband; and arXiv:2609.33869 Heavy Higgsino Dark Matter With Low Reheating in View of the LZ High-Recoil Event, which shows low-reheating with T_rh <=595 GeV can accommodate >1.1 TeV masses. Canonical thermal-mass references include arXiv:2205.04486, arXiv:1411.6930, arXiv:1912.07795 and arXiv:1104.0228. Direct-detection limits are from LZ 2024 arXiv:2410.17036 and XENONnT arXiv:2303.14729, with the xenon neutrino fog from XLZD arXiv:2410.17137. Indirect limits are from Fermi-LAT dwarf work arXiv:1611.03184 and related line searches, and CTAO-North projections.

## Results

### Thermal relic density versus Planck

The server tool reports Planck Omega h^2 = 0.12 +/-0.0012 and computes perturbative freeze-out with x_f ~24.4-24.8, T_f ~36.3 GeV at 900 GeV to 53.2 GeV at 1300 GeV, and sigma_v scaling ~1/m_chi^2 as 3.73e-26 cm3/s at 900 GeV to 1.79e-26 cm3/s at 1300 GeV. The grid is Omega h^2 = 0.0731 (900 GeV), 0.0898 (1000 GeV), 0.1083 (1100 GeV), 0.1181 (1150 GeV), 0.1202 (1160 GeV), 0.1285 (1200 GeV), 0.1503 (1300 GeV). Linear interpolation between 1150 GeV and 1160 GeV gives a thermal mass of 1159 GeV where Omega h^2 = 0.120, with the 1160 GeV point itself at 0.1202 within 0.1 sigma of Planck. The tool has no Sommerfeld enhancement, no bound-state formation and no coannihilation delta-dependence, so this 1159 GeV value is perturbative only and not independently verified against the literature Sommerfeld+bound-state values.

At m_chi = 1100 GeV the tool uses v_esc+v_E = 776 km/s and gives delta_max ~364 keV on xenon. Predicted kinematics are: delta = 200 keV peaks at E_R = 180 keV with v_min at peak 572 km/s and v_min at 248 keV = 579 km/s, accessible, predicting N = 51157.5 events in 2.84 tonne-yr with Poisson probability 1.0; delta = 350 keV peaks at 315.1 keV with v_min 757 km/s and v_min at 248 keV = 762 km/s, accessible, predicting N = 1.97 events with Poisson probability 0.86; delta = 500 keV peaks at 450.1 keV with v_min 905 km/s and v_min at 248 keV = 945 km/s, inaccessible, predicting N = 0.0.
